scope: Public-source organization discovery context only. No organization is asserted to be exposed or compromised.

incident_baseline.summary: PingCAP says stolen service credentials enabled internal access September 9–October 7. Exported records included account/organization/project information, SQL-editor text/errors, business/billing data, and encrypted API-key values. Customer scope remained under investigation; no evidence of impact to data stored in TiDB was found. Identified compromised credentials and access paths were remediated by October 14.
incident_baseline.japanese_access_note: Direct web open returned inaccessible; source text obtained through indexed web search on review date.
incident_baseline.japanese_summary: Japanese notice reports up to approximately 50,000 personal-information records in Japan and no confirmed unauthorized TiDB Cloud access or credit-card exposure. These are Japan-specific statements, not Hong Kong impact counts.

api_material_discrepancy.english: Encrypted TiDB Cloud API-key values were exported; one investigator-owned value could not be used directly. Whether other usable credentials were exposed remains unresolved, and support-material claims were unverified.
api_material_discrepancy.japanese: Says encrypted API public-key portions were exposed, private-key portions were not, and the exposed public portions alone cannot operate TiDB Cloud; recommends API-key rotation.
api_material_discrepancy.interpretation: Statements differ in scope and certainty. Preserve both attributions; neither demonstrates that every credential-like value in supplied files is usable or harmless. No authentication attempts are warranted.

interpretation_rules: Public business relationships are candidate discovery evidence, never breach evidence.
Separate CRM mentions, accounts, service usage, and sensitive-data exposure; none alone proves compromise of customer systems.
Distinguish self-managed TiDB, TiDB Cloud, and partner-console usage.
Do not infer downstream customers are exposed from reseller records.
Match organizational domains with exact/domain-boundary logic; incidental text and individual email domains require corroboration.
